posts.title: BetaFPV 95X V3 Over Water: The Settings, Battery, and Retest Plan
posts.excerpt: My second day with the BetaFPV 95X V3 produced a cinematic over-water flight—and questions about ISO, Log color, a 450mAh 4S pack, flight time, and acro practice that are still worth answering.

editorial.evidenceSummary: This article is grounded in Colin's exact January 2021 BetaFPV 95X V3 flight, its public description, and Colin's own visible replies about ISO 100, automatic settings, Log capture, DaVinci color correction, a 450mAh 4S pack, approximately 2.5-3 minutes in wind, and VelociDrone acro practice. Current BETAFPV and FAA pages were reviewed for forward-looking configuration and flight context. The archive does not preserve a complete build, raw-file metadata, controlled endurance test, exact route, or every camera and export setting, so the draft does not claim a definitive review, comparison, or recommendation.

data.text: I still like the nerve and calm in this flight. I also know an old cinematic edit is not the same thing as a complete test record. The useful story lives in the space between those two truths.

On New Year's Day 2021, during my second day with the BetaFPV 95X V3 and Insta360 SMO 4K, I took the little cinewhoop over water and showed my dad what it could do. Another pilot's over-water video had given me the push to try it. My upload preserved the flight; the conversation under it preserved several details I should have put in the description from the start.

data.text: This is a first-person archive reconstruction from my exact public upload and my own visible replies. It is not a recovered flight log. I do not have a complete build sheet, raw-file metadata, a standardized battery test, or every camera and export setting in this package. Nobody paid for placement, and there are no affiliate links in this draft.

items: The video is real second-day field footage, not a controlled product review or long-range test.
In a public reply, I said I locked ISO at 100, left the remaining settings automatic, shot in Log, and color corrected in DaVinci Resolve.
In another reply, I identified a 450mAh 4S pack and roughly 2.5-3 minutes of flight time in windy conditions.
I learned acro in VelociDrone and needed a couple of months before I felt comfortable; that is personal context, not a training prescription.
A proper retest would preserve the exact build, camera screen, source files, airspace check, weather, route, start/end voltage, and a planned reserve.

data.text: The distinction matters because BETAFPV's archived Beta95X V3 frame-kit page describes a 100 mm pusher/ducted frame and support for a lightweight SMO 4K camera, while its Beta95X V3 CLI archive lists controller, Betaflight, and motor-era variants. Those official pages help identify the product family; they do not reconstruct my complete aircraft.
The Acro Practice Behind the Line

When a viewer asked about the flight mode, I explained that I had learned acro in VelociDrone, made myself keep practicing it, and needed a couple of months before I became comfortable. I also said I was still practicing and did not consider myself a freestyle pilot. That humility belongs in the story: simulator time can support repetition, but it does not remove the need for a conservative real-world plan.
The Retest I Would Run Now

items: Record the exact aircraft, motor, controller, firmware, tune, receiver, propeller, battery, all-up weight, and camera mount.
Show the complete camera settings screen and name the stabilization, color, exposure, resolution, and frame-rate choices.
Check current operating rules and airspace for the exact location; use the FAA's current B4UFLY starting point where applicable.
Choose a short visual-line-of-sight route with a dry launch, a dry alternate landing area, no uninvolved people in the line, and a co-located observer when needed.
Start with a dry-ground hover and control check before any water-adjacent pass.
Log wind, pack condition, start voltage, end voltage, flight duration, and the reserve decision instead of flying until the footage feels finished.
Change one camera or aircraft variable per pass and repeat the same conservative line only when conditions remain suitable.
Preserve one named source clip, the unedited flight log, the color grade, stabilization pass, and export settings together.
Stop at the planned reserve or first sign of an aircraft, link, battery, weather, visibility, people, or recovery concern.

data.text: An Old Flight Is Not Current Authorization

For a present-day recreational U.S. flight, begin with the FAA's Recreational Flyers guidance and Where Can I Fly? page, determine which rules apply, check current airspace and authorization, and account for registration, Remote ID, visual-line-of-sight, community-based safety, property, state, and local requirements for the exact operation.

Do not copy an old over-water route from a cinematic edit. This article is not flight instruction, legal advice, airspace authorization, a waterproofing claim, or proof that a past flight met every current requirement.
Why I Still Like This Flight

It was my second day with the aircraft. I had been inspired by another pilot, wanted to show my dad, and brought home a line that still feels calm and committed. That human reason is stronger than turning the upload into a retroactive product verdict.
Keep the feeling from the old flight. Upgrade the evidence, exit plan, and reserve before the next one.

That is the Captain Colin standard I want to carry forward: real flights, exact limits, useful notes, and a next test the audience can help shape.
